therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: PD-1 checkpoint inhibition combined with radiation-induced immunogenic cell death
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: T-cell activation and anti-tumor immune response enhancement through checkpoint blockade and radiation-induced antigen release
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Previously treated patients with Stage IV NSCLC
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Number of Patients With Each Response as Measured by RECIST 1.1

results.effect_size: CR: 0 patients, PR: 4 patients, SD: 2 patients, PD: 5 patients, Other: 2 patients
biomarker_changes: PD-L1 negative patients: median OS 7.1 months (95% CI: 4.7–NA)
PD-L1 positive patients: median OS 13 months (95% CI: 2.1–NA)
subgroup_findings: PD-L1 positive patients showed longer median OS (13 vs 7.1 months) compared to PD-L1 negative patients
safety_signals: Serious adverse events included abdominal pain, cerebral edema, dyspnea, pleural effusion, death, fever, confusion, fall, acute kidney injury, respiratory failure
results.dose_information: Pembrolizumab 200mg IV infusion; Single fraction radiation therapy 8Gy

context.duration: Up to 24 months treatment and follow-up
